reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is an identifiable SmartCon stage presentation in which an OKX representative explains X Layer blockchain infrastructure and its integration with related products and protocols. The USDG rewards statement, APY figures, and ecosystem-fund invitation are presented as product and builder-support features, without described deceptive terms, guaranteed returns, required transfers, or completed transactions.

citations.quote: My name is Jason Lau. I'm Chief Innovation Officer at OKx.
So today here, I'm here to talk about X-Layer.
we invite you to come reach out to us and talk about that with us.
today, if you hold USDG on X layer within the OKEx wallet, again, this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to. You get to receive rewards on top of that.

opening.argument: The presentation links a passive financial benefit to a concrete wallet-and-asset action. The speaker says users who hold USDG on X Layer in the OKX wallet “get to receive rewards on top of that,” while the displayed product makes the offer operational by pairing “Hold USDG” with “Earn up to 4.1% APY” and an “Activate rewards” button. That is not merely discussion of blockchain infrastructure: it presents a return-bearing arrangement in which participation requires holding a specified stablecoin and activating the reward feature. The benefit is therefore tied to custody and wallet use, with the audience being directed toward a particular platform pathway.

citations.quote: today, if you hold USDG on X layer within the OKEx wallet, again, this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to. You get to receive rewards on top of that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a stage presentation does not resolve the substantive offer. The relevant evidence is the pairing of a specific holding requirement with rewards and activation, not whether the speaker introduces himself or names the event. The invitation to engage with the ecosystem also shows that the presentation is designed to move participants toward the platform and its products.

citations.quote: today, if you hold USDG on X layer within the OKEx wallet, again, this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to. You get to receive rewards on top of that.
we invite you to come reach out to us and talk about that with us.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence establishes a promotional reward feature, but it does not establish deception. The speaker describes the assets as self-custody, and the slide says “up to” 4.1% rather than guaranteeing a fixed return. Nothing shown states that viewers must transfer funds to the speaker, surrender keys, or pay a fee. A wallet feature linked to holding USDG is not by itself proof of a scam.

citations.quote: again, this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: crypto assets, a wallet-based rewards program, and prominent percentage yields. One slide displays “Earn up to 4.1% APY” for holding USDG and includes an activation control; another displays “Earn 5% APY” beside an OKX Pay payment interface. The speaker also says rewards are available for USDG held in the OKX wallet. Presenting multiple yield figures across payment and wallet products can make the offer look simple and readily accessible while leaving the material supplied here silent on duration, funding requirements, eligibility, source of yield, or loss conditions. That combination is sufficient to treat the promotion as a high-risk investment-style solicitation rather than neutral technical education.

citations.quote: today, if you hold USDG on X layer within the OKEx wallet, again, this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to. You get to receive rewards on top of that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The event setting and technical language do not answer the missing-terms problem. The reference account emphasizes that there is no stated guarantee or completed transaction, but a solicitation can still be risky when it foregrounds yields and directs users to hold assets and activate rewards. The “up to” wording limits the claim; it does not explain the conditions behind it.

citations.quote: You get to receive rewards on top of that.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual slides show product concepts, not proof of an investment pool, staking arrangement, or deceptive return scheme. “Earn up to 4.1% APY” and “Earn 5% APY” do not show the terms, source, or availability, but that absence cuts against an allegation of deception as much as it cuts against confidence in the offer. The speaker does not claim guaranteed profit or describe a required transfer.

citations.quote: this is self-custody assets that you hold the keys to.

opening.argument: Although framed as a conference talk about X Layer, the presentation functions as product promotion. It highlights trading, payments, wallet rewards, an ecosystem fund, and invitations to builders, repeatedly connecting participation with OKX’s network. In particular, the speaker says USDG holders in the OKX wallet receive rewards, while the slides present APY figures and an activation button. The technical framing gives these financial features institutional credibility, but the audience is still being steered toward a platform, a wallet, and return-bearing products. The presentation therefore should be evaluated by the concrete financial inducements it makes, not only by its conference setting or infrastructure vocabulary.

citations.quote: So today here, I'm here to talk about X-Layer.
On the wallet side too, xLayer is going to be a core piece of how users can earn and get rewarded for their assets in self-custody.
we invite you to come reach out to us and talk about that with us.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presentation’s educational appearance cannot neutralize its calls to participate. It promotes OKX’s products, describes users earning rewards through the wallet, displays APY claims, and invites people to engage with the ecosystem. Those are commercial inducements embedded in the technical explanation, so the conference setting is context rather than a defense.

citations.quote: xLayer is going to be a core piece of how users can earn and get rewarded for their assets in self-custody.
we invite you to come reach out to us and talk about that with us.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The talk does promote OKX products, but promotion is not equivalent to a scam. The reference evidence identifies the speaker and subject, and the reward statement describes holding self-custody assets rather than sending money to an unknown operator. The slides show product messaging, but they do not establish false claims, guaranteed returns, concealed fees, or a required investment transfer.
